title: Cigarroa Says She Will Skip Nov. 18 Mayoral Debate, Citing Fairness Concerns
excerpt: Mayoral candidate and District 8 Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa announced Tuesday night she will not take part in the Nov. 18 debate hosted by the City of Laredo, saying she has concerns about the fairness and impartiality of the city-run event, according to Hammrod News Laredo TX. She said she will take part in a Dec. 8 debate hosted by the Laredo Chamber of Commerce and airing on KGNS.
content:
Mayoral candidate and District 8 Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa announced Tuesday night, Nov. 17, that she will not take part in the Nov. 18 debate hosted by the City of Laredo, citing concerns about fairness and impartiality, according to Hammrod News Laredo TX, which reported her announcement.

In her announcement, Cigarroa said the city has shown preferential treatment toward incumbent Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño, including through its official social media platforms, and argued the circumstances raised serious concerns about the city’s ability to conduct a fair and impartial debate, according to the report. Webb Watch has not independently verified those claims, and the announcement did not provide specific examples of how the Nov. 18 debate’s questions, moderation or rules would favor either candidate, according to the report.

Cigarroa previously missed the Oct. 8 city-hosted mayoral forum, reportedly because of a prior engagement. She did take part in the Oct. 7 Chamber of Commerce forum and the Oct. 14 TAMIU debate, according to The Bridge, the Texas A&M International University student newspaper.

Comments were reportedly disabled on Cigarroa’s announcement, preventing residents from responding publicly beneath the post, according to Hammrod. The report noted the restriction is particularly noteworthy given that her statement emphasized listening to Laredoans, answering their questions and remaining accessible to the community.

Despite withdrawing from the Nov. 18 event, Cigarroa said she will participate in the Dec. 8 debate hosted by the Laredo Chamber of Commerce and airing on KGNS, according to the report.

Treviño and Cigarroa face off in a mayoral runoff on Dec. 12 after no candidate won more than 50 percent of the vote on Nov. 3, with early voting running Nov. 30 through Dec. 8, according to KGNS.

Sources: Hammrod News Laredo TX, Nov. 17, 2026; The Bridge, Nov. 3, 2026; KGNS, Nov. 4, 2026.
